title: Arrange, Act, Assert - in that order
brief:
This test fails, and not because the shop is broken. Run it first and read the message - it tells you exactly which page it was looking at.

Then fix it. Do not add anything: just put the three beats in the right order.
starter:
from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_products_link_opens_the_products_page(page: Page):
    # ARRANGE
    page.goto("https://automationexercise.com/")

    # ASSERT
    expect(page).to_have_url("https://automationexercise.com/products")

    # ACT
    page.get_by_role("link", name="Products").click()
solution:
from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_products_link_opens_the_products_page(page: Page):
    # ARRANGE
    page.goto("https://automationexercise.com/")

    # ACT
    page.get_by_role("link", name="Products").click()

    # ASSERT
    expect(page).to_have_url("https://automationexercise.com/products")

checks.label: The click actually happened and moved the shop to /products
checks.feedback: The shop is not on the products page at the end of your test. Did the click line run - or is it still sitting after the assertion?

checks.name: to_have_url
checks.label: You still assert the URL
checks.feedback: The expect(page).to_have_url(...) line has gone missing. Move it, do not delete it.

checks.label: You click the Products link
checks.feedback: No click reached the page. The Act step is what makes this a test of the link rather than a test of the home page.

hints.label: Nudge
hints.text: Read the failure. It says the URL it found was the home page. When was the assertion checked - before or after the click?

hints.label: Strategy
hints.text: Python runs top to bottom. Swap the ASSERT block and the ACT block so the check happens after the thing it is checking.

reveal:
An assertion that runs before the action is not a strict test - it is a test of the wrong moment. Playwright's auto-waiting will not save you here either: `to_have_url` retried for five seconds on a URL that was never going to change.

When a test fails, the first question is always **when did it check?**
